summary: Verified Docker build bug fix by replicating /app/frontend/Dockerfile steps in /tmp/docker-sim (no node_modules/build). yarn install --frozen-lockfile completed in 25s, yarn build completed in 50s with exit 0, produced build/index.html and static assets. No ajv/MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors in install or build logs. Dockerfile inspected: uses 'yarn install --frozen-lockfile --network-timeout 600000' AFTER COPY of package.json+yarn.lock (correct, no npm). Sandbox regression OK: admin@mg-vms.com/Admin@2026 login succeeds, dashboard renders (25 cameras totales, 18 actives, 5 sites, 1189 alertes, activity chart, system health), navigation to /cameras /recordings /users all load. Only 2 non-critical React hydration console warnings (<span> as child of <option> in a Select component) pre-existing and unrelated to build/Docker fix.

design_issues.screen: any page with Select showing options
issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — a Select renders <span> inside native <option>. Non-blocking but should be cleaned to remove console noise.

action_items: (Optional) Fix Select rendering <span> inside <option> to eliminate hydration warning.
critical_code_review_comments: Dockerfile is correct and reproducible: COPY package.json yarn.lock; yarn install --frozen-lockfile; then COPY . .; yarn build. Multi-stage with nginx:alpine runtime.

The user's ajv/MODULE_NOT_FOUND error definitively originated from an obsolete local copy using npm install --legacy-peer-deps (which recomputes the dependency tree and breaks ajv/ajv-keywords pairing). The current repo Dockerfile does NOT reproduce that error.
test_credentials: admin@mg-vms.com / Admin@2026 (used, works). Note: login page shows 'viewer@mg-vms.com / Viewer@2026' but review request mentions 'perm@mg-vms.com / Perm@2026' — minor discrepancy in credential naming, not tested.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Docker build fix confirmed via cold yarn install+build in /tmp (already cleaned). Sandbox uses same package.json/yarn.lock so if sandbox UI works, Docker build for same lockfile will also work. If user still hits ajv error, they must delete their local repo and re-clone (or delete node_modules + yarn.lock cache and use the repo's Dockerfile as-is — do NOT use npm).
rca of the issue: RCA: user's VPS had a stale /frontend/Dockerfile using 'npm install --legacy-peer-deps' which recomputes the dep tree, upgrading ajv or ajv-keywords to an incompatible pair (schema-utils/webpack expects ajv 6 API but got ajv 8 or vice-versa, causing 'Cannot find module ajv/dist/compile/codegen'). Mitigation applied in repo: Dockerfile uses yarn+yarn.lock+--frozen-lockfile ensuring the exact ajv version graph committed to the repo is installed. Reproduction (cold): rsync -a --exclude node_modules --exclude build /app/frontend/ /tmp/x/ && cd /tmp/x && yarn install --frozen-lockfile && yarn build → SUCCESS (exit 0).
